verdicts.reason: Y only lifts the consequence requirement from the 10-anchor into the lead sentence; the anchors are otherwise word-for-word identical, so scores would be interchangeable.
Both require naming a specific overlap, contradiction, gap, or sequencing problem with another instrument plus a resolution, and both zero out isolated analysis.
Identical property (practical steps, resources, timing, personnel, supply-chain) with the same 10 and 0 anchors, only reordered into a one-line form.
Both score whether a concrete, implementable alternative regulatory design is offered, with 0 for mere objection or silence.
The same surface register list drives both scales; Y just omits the explanatory note that the register, not its warrant, is being scored.
Both score the traceability of the derivation from stated evidence to the exact provision or action requested, with identical 10 and 0 anchors.
Both require commenter-derived compliance-cost figures with the basis stated; the dollar framing in Y is how compliance cost is expressed in X, so the scores track.
Both score relevant numerical data, calculations, comparisons, or rates supporting the position, with 0 for no verifiable quantitative support.
X scores emotional register while Y scores first-hand operational experience; a flat, detailed practitioner account scores 0 on X and 10 on Y.
Both score presence of prior or ongoing agency-relationship cues with the same enumerated markers; Y adds only a surface-feature reminder.
Both score the same document-production packaging signals with the same 10 and 0 anchors; Y adds only a surface-feature reminder.
Both require a specific alternative, exception, phase-in, or substitute plus an explanation of how it meets the same objective with tradeoffs named.
Both score weighing benefits against costs, risks, displaced protections, or unintended effects, with 0 for one-sided support or opposition.
The same templated activist markers and structure define both scales; Y only reorders them and adds a surface-feature note about sincerity.
Both score the same itemized, addressee-directed, rule-section-citing rebuttal layout against continuous persuasive prose; Y drops only an illustrative example.
All three anchors match in substance: reworked agency arithmetic or juxtaposition with the agency's own record at 10, unsupported dispute at 5, preference-only at 0.
Both require naming particular differently situated groups and explaining the mechanism, with 0 for undifferentiated public-interest appeals.
The beneficiary-of-the-ask construct and all three anchors are preserved verbatim in substance; only clause order differs.
Y spells out in the 0-anchor what X's 10-anchor already implies, that an unspecified allegation does not count; the property scored is the same demonstrated internal conflict.
Both score letter casing alone with identical wholly-or-almost-wholly-capitals versus sentence-case anchors.
Both score a traced chain from provision through behavior or implementation to a consequence; X's 'each link stated' and Y's 'credible chain' are the same demand for intervening steps.
Both score self-imposed limits: circumstances where the commenter's own recommendation fails or evidence that would change it, 0 when absent.
Both score only the verbatim presence of a docket identifier or RIN string, with the same explicit exclusion of rule-relevance judgments.
All three anchors are substantively identical: standard named with elements matched to facts at 10, implicit application at 5, quotation or no standard at 0.
Both score whether evidentiary limits are marked and whether the recommendation responds to them, with the same 10, 5, and 0 anchors.
Both score the register shift of a formal citation embedded in informal first-person prose, with the same 0 for uniform register or no citation.
Both score a prominent opening display of degrees, certifications, offices, titles, or years of experience; Y omits only the surface-feature reminder.
X scores presence of part/section CFR citations while Y scores a developed statutory-authority argument; a citation-dense comment making no authority claim scores high on X and 0 on Y.
Both score how prominently the writer discloses identity, credentials, role, or stake, and both explicitly set aside whether that identity is load-bearing.
